thread:
maria_sec: Heads-up: starting 2026-12-14T07:00Z we saw a spike (~1.7k) of TLS handshake rejects from ap-northeast -> svc-analytics. Errors show client cert CN=svc-analytics-old and some cipher negotiation failures. Might be tied to the RBAC regroup last week.

keystore-rotator-bot: rotator: completed rotation job keystore-analytics-aps-20261214-01 at 2026-12-14T03:29:58Z (principal=rotator-sa@infra.redwood). No errors reported by rotator.

tom_sre: ingress sample: 
```
2026-12-14T06:59:57Z ingress-aps-01 svc-analytics=\"svc-analytics-01\" tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate (client CN=svc-analytics-old, expected svc-analytics)
2026-12-14T07:00:03Z ingress-aps-02 svc-analytics=\"svc-analytics-02\" tls: handshake error: tls: unsupported protocol or cipher suite
```

yara_infra: KMS audit for key keystore-analytics-aps around rotation window (03:28-03:32Z):
```
{"timestamp":"2026-12-14T03:29:59Z","principal":"svc-analytics-old@infra.redwood","action":"Decrypt","resource":".../keystore-analytics-key"}
{"timestamp":"2026-12-14T03:30:01Z","principal":"rotator-sa@infra.redwood","action":"Decrypt","resource":".../keystore-analytics-key"}
```

maria_sec: So legacy SA still had decrypt rights and could have minted certs during rollout. That explains CN mismatch and mixed cipher behavior if old certs use older keymaterial/profile.

devex-lex: Quick mitigation + hardening suggestions (short):
- Remove orphan IAM binding for svc-analytics-old from KMS (infra).
- Rerun a canary rotation with rotator-sa only and verify CNs.
- Add alert: any KMS Decrypt on keystore-* by principals not in allowlist -> page sec-oncall.
- Rotator pre-check: fetch KMS IAM policy before rotation, fail-canary if unexpected principals exist.
- TLS config hardening: enforce TLS1.3, disable RSA key exchange, prefer AEAD ciphers, enable OCSP stapling and short stapled responses for certs used in mTLS.
- Add a quick CI/integration that runs `openssl s_client -connect svc-analytics.aps.internal:443 -tlsextdebug` against a canary to assert CN and TLS protocol.

maria_sec: Owners: yara for KMS IAM removal, tom for canary/runbook, lex for creating alert and rotator RFC, sec to file incident. Can we action now?

yara_infra: Removing legacy binding now and will reconcile terraform state.

keystore-rotator-bot: rotator: starting canary rotation job keystore-analytics-aps-20261214-canary using rotator-sa@infra.redwood

yara_infra: Legacy binding removed @2026-12-14T07:15:20Z. Verified IAM policy no longer includes svc-analytics-old. Will open PR to purge orphan state entry.

keystore-rotator-bot: rotator: canary rotation completed at 2026-12-14T03:31:10Z. Issued certs with CN=svc-analytics and profile=tls1.3-only.

tom_sre: Quick probe from ap-northeast: `openssl s_client -connect svc-analytics.aps.internal:443 -tlsextdebug -status` returns client cert CN=svc-analytics and TLSv1.3 handshake OK. Rejects dropped to baseline by 07:18Z.

devex-lex: Follow-ups: 1) I'll open the alert PR and add a weekly decrypt-principals dashboard; 2) I'll draft the rotator IAM pre-check RFC and make it a safe default; 3) infra to purge terraform orphan entry and add an IAM parity CI check.

maria_sec: Filing P2 incident with root cause = leftover project-level IAM binding after RBAC consolidation; contributing factors = no pre-rotation IAM sanity and lack of KMS-decrypt alerts. Also adding TLS hardening notes to runbook (TLS1.3 enforcement + OCSP stapling).

keystore-rotator-bot: note: rotation audit artifacts uploaded to gs://redwood-infra-rotator/audits/keystore-analytics-20261214-canary.json

tom_sre: Thanks team. If anyone sees similar spikes in other regions, copy this checklist and ping sec-oncall. :thumbsup:
